props.title: Modern Collective
props.initialSlug: Pro surfers redefine modern surf style & culture

sections.content: **Modern Collective** (2009) revolutionized surf filmmaking by ditching the traditional "endless summer" narrative for a raw, youth-driven perspective. Director Kai Neville captured a new generation of surfers including Dane Reynolds and Jordy Smith with frenetic editing and punk energy that influenced countless surf films after. Like **Momentum** (1992) did for the 90s, Modern Collective defined progressive surfing for the late 2000s through innovative angles and a gritty aesthetic that felt more **Kids** (1995) than **Endless Summer** (1966).

sections.content: The film's impact extended beyond just surf culture. Its quick-cut style and electronic soundtrack influenced action sports filmmaking broadly, seen in later works like **The Art of Flight** (2011) and **We Are Blood** (2015). Neville's approach treated surfing as an urban sport rather than a beach lifestyle, shooting in gritty locations and focusing on technical progression over soul surfing.

Modern Collective marked a clear break from surf film tradition established by **Morning of the Earth** (1971) and **Crystal Voyager** (1973). Instead of mystical narration and extended wave-riding sequences, it emphasized explosive maneuvers and rapid-fire editing that matched the intensity of contemporary skateboard videos like **Fully Flared** (2007). sections.content: The film's digital-first approach predicted how surf media would evolve in the 2010s. While earlier surf films were made for theater and DVD releases, Modern Collective embraced web clips and social media, influencing how **Strange Rumblings in Shangri La** (2014) and **Cluster** (2015) would later be both filmed and distributed.
